children: Candel Therapeutics reported positive Phase 3 disease-free survival results in intermediate- to high-risk localized prostate cancer and encouraging survival and safety data across NSCLC and recurrent high-grade glioma programs.
Phase 3 prostate cancer trial (n=745) met primary DFS endpoint: 30% risk reduction (HR 0.70; P=0.0155) vs placebo plus SOC.
Prostate cancer-specific DFS improved 38% (HR 0.62; P=0.0046); median follow-up 50.3 months; higher 2‑yr pCR (80% vs 63%; P=0.0018).
Prostate safety profile favorable: lower incidence of SAEs (5.8% vs 7.3%) and treatment‑related SAEs (1.7% vs 2.2%); most TRAEs grade 1–2.
NSCLC phase 2a showed mOS up to 25.4 months (per‑protocol) and 21.5 months in progressive disease cohort, with durable responses and abscopal effects.
Linoserpaturev in recurrent high‑grade glioma showed encouraging survival versus expected medians (<6–9 mos) and immune remodeling; repeated dosing feasible and well tolerated.
